agent: wave reader A, start technology from the data side
question: Who gives a new game's countries technology levels their history does not, and by what rule? Every writer of CTechnologyStatus +0x218 sorted, and the one that is none of research, history, script, commands or the custom game read whole.

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel(int level@ECX, CTechnology* technology@EDX, CTechnologyStatus* status@stack:4, bool recordHistory@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **Sets a country's level of one technology, the history's way.** level_by_technology (+0x218)[technology->Index (+0x244)] = min(level, max_level (+0x2C4)). With recordHistory set it also builds a CTechnologyChange (0x1C bytes, CTechnologyChange::CTechnologyChange then SetLevel), stamps it with the current tick (CHistoryEntry +0x8 = gamestate +0xBDC) and hands it to the country's history (CCountry +0xCCC, slot 6). No ApplyTechnologyEffects, no progress, no ability. `ret 8` at VA 0x5332AC. Two callers, both in CTechnologyChange::Apply, both with recordHistory 0 - so a history file's `technology` block reaches the levels here.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x533190-0x5332AC; ecx and edx are used before being written (`mov edi, edx`, `mov esi, ecx`), the status is [ebp+8] and the flag [ebp+0xC], `ret 8`. The record's flag reading rests on the two callers passing 0 and the branch building a CTechnologyChange. Wrong if a third caller passed the arguments otherwise.

addresses.name: CTechnologyChange::CTechnologyChange
addresses.signature: CTechnologyChange* __thiscall CTechnologyChange::CTechnologyChange(CTechnologyChange* this, CCountry* country, CTechnology* technology)
addresses.comment: Calls CCountryHistoryEntry::CCountryHistoryEntry with the country, writes vftable 0x15C9760 (VA), sets technology (+0x10) and zeroes level (+0x14) and previous_level (+0x18). `ret 8`. Two callers: CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel (VA 0x5331F2) and CCountryHistory::LoadEntry (VA 0x5EE448), which is how a history file's `technology` block becomes a change.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole (0x5EEE40-0x5EEE7F); the table written is the one the RTTI export gives CTechnologyChange. The LoadEntry attribution is functionStart plus the record's entry for 0x1ECA90; the call's surroundings were not read.

addresses.name: CTechnologyChange::Apply
addresses.comment: Slot 7, the history change's Apply. forward: previous_level (+0x18) = the country's current level (CTechnologyStatus::GetLevel), then CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel(level +0x14, technology +0x10, country->technology_status, 0). Backward: SetLevel(previous_level, ...). So the history's `technology` levels are set and undone here, without effects - those come later from ReapplyAllTechnologies.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole (0x5EEEB0-0x5EEF48, `ret 4`); vtable.py --holding puts it at CTechnologyChange slot 7 and nowhere else, as the other XChange::Apply are.

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus_Clear
addresses.comment: For every technology of the database: level (+0x218), progress (+0x228, eight bytes) and assigned leadership (+0x238) set to 0. It then walks the unit-type database (0x1A886F0), which was not read. `ret 4` at VA 0x532223. One caller, CCountry_Reset (VA 0x4D483E).
addresses.evidence: Only the first loop (VA 0x532082-0x532114) was read; the rest of the body and so the whole of what it clears is not. The name rests on that loop and the caller.

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus_RevertDisallowedLevels
addresses.comment: Custom game. For every technology whose current level CheckResearchAllowed refuses and that is above 0: level set to 0 (min(0, max_level)), progress zeroed, and its entry in the country's research list (CCountry +0x638) taken out; with `log` a line goes to technology.cpp. A changed flag suggests it repeats until nothing changes. `ret 8` at VA 0x533946. Four callers, all custom-game code: CCgmTechResearchChangeCommand, CCgmTechResearchResetCommand and CCgmTechResearchExecuteStackedCommand slot 6, and VA 0x419FD7.
addresses.evidence: The test and the write read (VA 0x533584-0x5338E4); the logging body and the loop's restart were not followed. Callers by findRefs; holders by vtable.py.

addresses.name: CgmTechSnapshot_RestoreTechnology
addresses.comment: Custom game: puts one technology back from a stored copy - the country is snapshot +4 (an id), its level becomes min(snapshot +8 [index], max_level) and its progress snapshot +0x18 [index]. Bare `ret`. One caller, CCgmTechResearchResetCommand slot 6 (VA 0x42B1FF).
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole (VA 0x41A320-0x41A3B5). What the snapshot object is was not read; its layout here is only what this body uses.

addresses.name: CgmTechSnapshot_RestoreAll
addresses.comment: Custom game: the same as CgmTechSnapshot_RestoreTechnology for every technology of the database. `ret 4` at VA 0x41A586. One caller, VA 0x41F836, after the custom-game settings getter 0x41F500.
addresses.evidence: The head and the write loop read (VA 0x41A3C0-0x41A520); the caller's purpose was not read.

structs.name: CTechnologyChange
structs.comment: A history change that sets one technology's level: what a `technology` block of a country history file becomes. Slot 7 is Apply.
structs.evidence: CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel allocates 0x1C for one (`push 0x1c` at VA 0x5331D7) before calling the constructor; the RTTI export gives CCountryHistoryEntry as its only base, at 0, and 0x15C9760 (VA) as its one table.

struct_fields.name: technology
struct_fields.comment: the technology whose level this change sets; the constructor's second argument
struct_fields.evidence: Written by the constructor at VA 0x5EEE62; read by Apply and passed in edx to CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel.

struct_fields.name: level
struct_fields.comment: the level set going forward; written by CTechnologyChange::SetLevel
struct_fields.evidence: SetLevel writes it; Apply(forward) passes it in ecx to CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel.

struct_fields.name: previous_level
struct_fields.comment: the level before this change, kept by Apply(forward) and set back by Apply(backward)
struct_fields.evidence: Apply(forward) stores CTechnologyStatus::GetLevel's answer here (VA 0x5EEEE8); Apply(backward) passes it to SetLevel (VA 0x5EEF37).

notes: Writers of CTechnologyStatus +0x218 entries, by a scan of every `mov reg, [x+0x218]` followed by a store through that register (callee-saved registers followed across calls): AdvanceResearch (research), CTechnologyStatus_SetLevel via CTechnologyChange::Apply (history), CTechnologyStatus::LoadKey 0x132230 (savegame), CTechnologyStatus_Clear (reset), ReleaseProvinces (a released country takes the oppressor's higher levels), SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame (the new-game head start), and six custom-game bodies. No script effect and no Lua call writes a level. Positive control: the scan finds AdvanceResearch's `inc`, ReleaseProvinces and LoadKey, all known before.

reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md says 'the assigner at rva 0xD59D0 ... recomputes entry +0 from relations and faction when a game is entered'; that is SetUpCountryForNewGame (0xD6230), which never runs on a load. reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md's 'the country's starting technology and not its laws' - it is both.
